clue.text: Wool knitted in Rome

indicators.note: knitted suggests strands worked together into a new pattern, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone knitting woollens while in Italy's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' rearranges IN ROME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine wool from a breed of sheep bearing that name.

clue.text: Minimal cover for a tanner, perhaps?

definitions.text: Minimal cover for a tanner, perhaps?

parts.words: Minimal cover for a tanner, perhaps?
parts.note: a tanner here is a sunbather, not a leather worker, and the skimpiest garment worn on the beach is meant

explanation.surface: A question about the least protection a leather-tanner might need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanner' suggests a leatherworker (or an old British sixpence), but it is someone getting a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit covers very little of a sunbather's body.

clue.text: Considerate chap has a smart turn-out as sovereign's bodyguard.

parts.note: considerate means gentle
a chap is a man

indicators.note: a turn-out here signals the letters of the following word being turned out into a new order

explanation.surface: A thoughtful fellow dresses smartly as a royal guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-out' reads as a smartly dressed appearance, but it is the anagram signal on 'smart'; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gentlemen-at-Arms are a ceremonial corps guarding the British monarch.

clue.text: Planetarium endlessly showing top billing

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a planetarium is a star dome

explanation.surface: A planetarium show earns headline status.
explanation.walkthrough: A planetarium is a STAR DOME; 'endlessly' cuts its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity status, the position of the star whose name heads the bill.

clue.text: For this second opinion, see doctor in Iran perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words could be arranged some other way, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Advice to seek another medical view from a physician in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges all fifteen letters of SEE DOCTOR IN IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking a matter over again produces a revised view.

clue.text: This gigantic creature is around no longer

indicators.note: no longer here signals the words are no longer in their original order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge beast that is extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of an extinct animal; 'no longer' rearranges IS AROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric reptile, many species of which were enormous.

clue.text: Asks advice of emissaries about time

indicators.note: about means the emissaries' word goes around the time letter

parts.note: consuls are officials sent to represent a state abroad

explanation.surface: Someone seeks guidance from envoys about timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside CONSULS.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek the opinion of someone is to turn to them for guidance.

clue.text: Deposit of ten cents sent round

indicators.note: round says the word sent is placed around the coin

parts.note: taken as written
a dime is a US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit by posting ten cents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' suggests a payment, which the coins in the surface encourage, but it is matter settling out of a liquid; a dime is the American ten-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit.

clue.text: Name of inventor noised abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An inventor's name being spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges NOISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison invented the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Section of the Circle Line from a familiar carriage?

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of the London Underground's Circle Line seen from a train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here a circle's line is its circumference. The letters sit across 'familiar carriage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved part of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Barrie's churchman — one in priory church

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, often one attached to a monastery or priory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman from J M Barrie's story sitting in a monastic church.
explanation.walkthrough: J M Barrie wrote The Little Minister; 'in' puts I inside MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman, as in the title of Barrie's novel about a young Scottish pastor.

clue.text: A producer for the symphony orchestra?

definitions.text: A producer for the symphony orchestra?

parts.words: A producer for the symphony orchestra?
parts.note: the producer is not someone staging the concert but a player who produces sound from a double-reed woodwind

explanation.surface: Asking who the orchestra's impresario is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producer' suggests a manager or promoter; here it is a musician producing notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe produces part of the orchestra's sound.

clue.text: Peeler could be best in cool place

indicators.note: could be hints the letters can become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peeling fruit, perhaps best done somewhere chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'peeler' is old British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the force. 'could be' rearranges BEST IN COOL PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Peel founded the Metropolitan Police, so officers were nicknamed after him.

clue.text: To beat, take iron from flame

indicators.note: take, with from, says the iron letters are removed from the word flame

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Instructions for beating metal: take the iron out of the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... from' removes FE from FLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is an informal verb meaning to thrash or hit hard.

clue.text: Cupholders may take cheer from it

definitions.text: Cupholders may take cheer from it

parts.words: Cupholders may take cheer from it
parts.note: people holding teacups draw their comforting drink from a large Russian tea urn

explanation.surface: Something that lifts the spirits of those holding cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer' is the cup that cheers, tea, served from a Russian urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian metal urn used to heat water for tea.

clue.text: A police-chief as drug-taker?

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
a chief is a head

explanation.surface: Asking whether a senior police officer takes drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the British police's detective branch, so its chief is the CID HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a habitual user of LSD, which is known as acid.

clue.text: Trample down, having finished with forest track

parts.note: something finished is over
a ride is a path cut through woodland for riding

explanation.surface: Someone finished on a forest path, trampling it down.
explanation.walkthrough: A RIDE is a British term for a track through a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride over is to trample, and overriding something tramples it underfoot.

clue.text: These days, put on formal clothes to make speech

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
to dress is to put on formal wear

explanation.surface: Nowadays you dress up to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno Domini) stands for the current era, 'these days'.
explanation.definitionFit: To address an audience is to deliver a speech to it.

clue.text: Form of the runic character

indicators.note: form of suggests a reshaped version of the next word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing the shape of an old runic letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old English and Icelandic letter for the th sound.

clue.text: Sole highwayman?

parts.note: a robber who works alone, read as one whose sole goes on the road, a robber on foot rather than horseback

explanation.surface: Asking about a lone robber of the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' suggests the only robber; it is the sole of the foot, for a highwayman who goes on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical name for a robber who preyed on travellers on foot, not on horseback.

clue.text: He may have camera right open, turning?

definitions.text: He may have camera right open, turning?

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of the preceding words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A film crew member keeping the camera rolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges CAMERA RIGHT OPEN; the whole clue also describes a filmmaker with the camera running.
explanation.definitionFit: The director of photography operates the film camera on a shoot.

clue.text: Overindulge a parliamentarian for every round

indicators.note: round says the word for every goes around the other pieces

parts.note: per means for each
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Spoiling an MP for each round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests a round of drinks, but it is the container signal: the 'for every' word wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to spoil someone with excessive comfort.

clue.text: Swinging trapezes, without exercise, is artificial

indicators.note: swinging trapezes move about, so these letters are rearranged once the exercise letters go

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Acrobats on trapezes skipping their workout, looking fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes PE from TRAPEZES, leaving TRAZES, which 'Swinging' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute, an imitation of the genuine thing.

clue.text: Native climber among the Esher pansies

indicators.note: among says the answer sits within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A climbing plant growing among pansies in Esher.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a town in Surrey; 'climber' suggests a plant, but it is a Himalayan mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherpas are a Himalayan people renowned as mountain guides.

clue.text: Does one put a brave face on religious objects?

definitions.text: Does one put a brave face on religious objects?

parts.words: Does one put a brave face on religious objects?
parts.note: a brave here is a Native American warrior, and the carved faces on a sacred pole are meant

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone stays stoic about sacred relics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave face' sounds like stoicism, but a brave is a Native American warrior whose face is carved on a totem pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in or carver of totems, sacred emblems of a clan.

clue.text: Rent not quite ready

indicators.note: not quite says the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: Rent payment not entirely ready yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money for housing but is a tear. 'not quite' drops the last letter of RIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear in fabric, which is a rip.

clue.text: Daisy's transport, going by air

parts.note: the song Daisy Bell, an air, has the line about a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A woman named Daisy flying somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going by air' suggests flying, but the air is a tune: the song Daisy Bell features a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle with seats for two riders, one behind the other.

clue.text: Lover-possibly Romeo at end of act

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters might be ordered otherwise, so they are rearranged
end of picks the final letter of the word act

explanation.surface: Romeo appearing as a lover at the close of an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ROMEO, AT and T (the last letter of 'act').
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cupid, a little love figure, or a lover.
